record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; code was not read or run. The README points to a separate paper, which is not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports that eight projection-ablation variants leave 90–100% refusal on this hybrid model, and contrasts that with constant displacement along the extracted direction. This is evidence challenging or refining the proposed ablation mechanism, rather than a reproduction of the original method.
record.gate_note: The README reports results for projection ablation, vector injection, random-vector control, injection site and timing, and served evaluations. The named scripts and harness steps are not evidence that unreported runs succeeded. SVD/probe details and individual projection-variant results are not reported in the README.
record.test_reason: On a hybrid mHC model, the README reports that projecting out the difference-in-means refusal direction (eight variants) leaves 90–100% refusal. It also reports that a random vector at a similar dose removes refusal as fully as the extracted direction. Both results bear directly on V1's causal-mediation claim. It also evaluates two community weight-edit abliterations (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add the authors' explicit magnitude/direction dissociation: displacement magnitude, even along a random vector, removes refusal, while the extracted direction only preserves capability. Also add that the shipped vectors are residual directions from an already-abliterated checkpoint, so the method tops up community abliterations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful/harmless activation differences to capture a direction, but reports constant injection rather than the original projection ablation; the main intervention is prefill-only and applied to selected sites in an mHC hybrid model. The README describes this as an agent-run abliteration study and points to a separate paper, not as a reproduction of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports sensitivity to injection dose, injection site/stream, prefill-only versus decode-time injection, and evaluation generation length. It also says the vectors are checkpoint- and precision-specific.

fits_no_version.finding: 200-token evaluations understate refusal compared with 1000-token evaluations on identical configurations (5%→20%, 0%→10%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured refusal-removal success depends on generation length; short evaluations overstate abliteration.

record.problems: The README reports a refusal set of 20 prompts, capability set of 10, single seed, greedy decoding, and marker-classifier scoring with one observed false positive. It cautions that 0% refusal is based on a thin sample. Individual projection-variant results and uncertainty estimates are not provided in the README.
record.rows_left_out: The README does not provide individual outcomes for the eight projection variants, numeric results for the other-stream or creativity findings, or detailed sweep/probe results; only the aggregate or qualitative summaries were recorded. The separate paper is not part of the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: README only; the formal paper is not included. The study is agent-run and not peer-reviewed. It uses a thin evaluation: 20 harmful and 10 capability prompts, single seed, marker classifier. The README cites the original as arXiv:2406.11732, not 2406.11717. Repository dates are in 2026. Interventions use negative doses, i.e. subtraction of the direction.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report adding the direction to harmless requests and measuring induced refusal. Capability testing is limited to 10 prompts; it does not establish that general abilities are largely intact. Projection variants are reported only as an aggregate.
Reports evaluations of community-abliterated checkpoints, but does not report making or releasing a weight edit itself, or a matched unedited-checkpoint comparison.
No attack that suppresses the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
No result compares an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions with a dominant direction.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision measurement is reported.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.
